introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography (0750), Paper 3, ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: three and a quarter hours.**

Answer FOUR questions in all. Answer question ONE and three others, choosing at least ONE question from SECTION B and TWO from SECTION C. Question ONE carries thirty-one marks and the rest carry twenty-three marks each.

Only the required number of questions will be marked.

In answering questions on this paper, you are encouraged to refer to your own field and practical work where relevant. Credit will be awarded for such references.

Candidates are advised NOT to attempt the questions on field investigations if such an exercise has not been carried out.

Marks will be awarded for well annotated maps and diagrams where these are relevant.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Calculators are allowed.

Materials required: Topographic map, graph paper and two outline maps of Cameroon.

figures.legende: Outline map of Cameroon with graticule ticks (10 degrees E and 16 degrees E; 2, 6, 10 and 12 degrees N), to be used for the location of forest resources in question 6(a).

Schematic model map for 6(a): dense humid forest in the south, forest-savanna mosaic belt to the north of it, and approximate positions of some protected forests (Korup, Mount Cameroon, Campo-Ma'an, Dja, Lobeke/Boumba-Bek/Nki, Kilum-Ijim, Benoue); positions and limits are approximate; produced for the model answer.

Les faits cités (régions, institutions, sites) sont ceux de la géographie du Cameroun couramment enseignée ; les chiffres sont arrondis et donnés avec « about » quand ils ne sont pas certains ; aucune statistique précise n'est avancée. À relire par un géographe avant mise en avant.

Les faits cités sont à vérifier avant mise en avant : noms d'institutions et de sites (par exemple Wakwa, Jakiri, Waza, Korup, Campo-Ma'an, Dja, Lobeke, SODECOTON, CICAM), séries chronologiques (insécurité du Nord depuis environ 2013-2014, abattage d'éléphants vers 2012) et ordres de grandeur ; tout chiffre précis a été omis ou donné avec « about ».

Question 6(a) : la carte fig-2 est SCHÉMATIQUE : les limites de la forêt dense (environ 4 à 6 degrés N selon la longitude) et de la mosaïque forêt-savane, et les positions des aires protégées sont approximatives, placées à partir du quadrillage de latitude et de longitude du fond de carte (10 et 16 degrés E ; 2, 6, 10 et 12 degrés N) ; elle illustre la méthode (zones ombrées, signes, légende, titre) et ne remplace pas un atlas. La proportion « environ 40 pour cent » du territoire sous forêt est un ordre de grandeur non vérifié.

Points imprimés : 6 + 6 + 6 + 5 = 23 (le sujet imprime (i) 6 et (ii) 6 ; le bloc b) est donc à 12).

questions.enonce_markdown:
6. a) Describe the spatial distribution of forest resources in Cameroon and locate them on the outline map provided. (6 marks)

![fig-1](gce-al-geography-2022-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Distribution (about 4 marks).**

- **Dense humid forest in the south (the main forest zone).** It covers the whole southern third of the country, in the South, East, Centre, Littoral and South-West Regions, from the Atlantic coast eastwards to the borders with Congo and the Central African Republic (about 40 per cent of the country's area is under forest, to be taken as an order of magnitude). It is part of the Congo Basin forest: evergreen forest near the coast, semi-deciduous forest further inland. This is the zone of the **timber** (for example ayous, sapele, iroko, ebony) and of the **non-timber products** (bush mango, njansang, rattan, medicinal plants), logged mostly in the East and the South with exports through Douala and Kribi.
- **Forest-savanna transition (mosaic)** north of the dense forest, roughly in the northern Centre, southern Adamawa and the West: patches of forest and savanna.
- **Montane and mountain forests** on the Western Highlands (for example the Kilum-Ijim forest on Mount Oku) and on Mount Cameroon.
- **Mangroves** on the coast (Douala estuary, Rio del Rey and the Bakassi area) and **gallery forests** along rivers in the savanna.
- **Woodland savanna** with scattered trees (a source of firewood and some timber) in the Adamawa and the north, with very little forest in the Sahelian Far North.
- **Protected forests**: national parks and reserves such as Korup, Mount Cameroon, Campo-Ma'an, Dja Faunal Reserve, and Lobeke, Boumba-Bek and Nki in the south-east, as well as many forest reserves and the Benoue woodland in the north.

**Map (about 2 marks).** On the outline map shade the dense forest zone in the south, add a lighter band for the mosaic, mark the main protected forests with a sign, and write a title and a key; label the main regions with their names.

![fig-2](gce-al-geography-2022-p3-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_2.png)

*Marks: description 4; map location, key and title 2. The limits on the model map are approximate.*

questions.enonce_markdown:
b) i) Examine TWO major tourist attractions in the northern part of Cameroon. (6 marks)

ii) Explain why tourists hardly visit them in recent times. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(b)(i) Two major attractions (6 marks, 3 each).**

1. **Waza National Park (Far North Region).** A large park of Sahelian savanna and seasonally flooded plains, famous for elephants, lions, giraffes and antelopes and for its large numbers of birds; visited by safari tours in the dry season (wildlife viewing and photography). Attractive because the animals gather at the waterholes in the dry season and the park lies close to the Logone floodplain and the lake Chad area.
2. **The Mandara Mountains and Rhumsiki (Far North Region).** A scenery of volcanic plugs (the spectacular Rhumsiki peak), with terraced farms, the traditional villages and craft of the Kapsiki and Mafa peoples, markets and festivals, and good hiking.

*(Other acceptable attractions: the Benoue and Bouba Njida National Parks, the Lagdo reservoir, the Lamidates (the palace of Rey Bouba), the craft centres of Maroua and Garoua.)*

**(b)(ii) Why tourists hardly visit in recent times (6 marks; any three well-explained reasons).**

- **Insecurity**: attacks and kidnappings by Boko Haram in the Far North and the North since about 2013-2014, and the banditry in the region, have made foreign governments advise their citizens against travel there; tour operators have cancelled their trips.
- **Poaching and decline of wildlife**: the killing of elephants and other animals reduces the main attraction of the parks.
- **Poor accessibility and weak facilities**: bad roads, few quality hotels and tourist services, high cost of transport and limited information, and the long distance from the main airports.
- **Other shocks**: the COVID-19 pandemic and, for the country as a whole, the socio-political crisis in the Anglophone regions, which damaged the image of the country.
- **Weak promotion**, and the decline of income of the local people who depended on tourism.

*Marks: attractions 3 + 3; reasons 6.*

questions.enonce_markdown: c) Examine the measures put in place to boost trade in Cameroon. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Measures (any five points explained, 1 mark each).**

1. **Transport and port infrastructure**: the building and upgrading of roads, railways and ports (for example the deep-sea port of Kribi and the extension of the Douala port) and of the corridors to Chad and the Central African Republic (Douala-Ngaoundere-N'Djamena), including the dry port at Ngaoundere.
2. **Regional integration**: membership of CEMAC and ECCAS, the African Continental Free Trade Area and the trade agreements with the European Union, which open larger markets and reduce tariffs.
3. **Customs and trade facilitation**: reforms of customs procedures, the one-stop shop for foreign trade, the reduction of delays and illegal checkpoints.
4. **Incentives and promotion**: the investment code, the industrial free zones and export incentives, trade fairs and export promotion agencies, support to small and medium enterprises.
5. **Diversification of exports and local processing** of agricultural products (cocoa, coffee, cotton, timber), the "Made in Cameroon" campaign, the construction of markets and cross-border trade posts, and measures against smuggling and counterfeit goods.

*Marks: measures named and explained.*
